newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: BHP plans to sell refractories operation.
newsitem.headline: BHP plans to sell refractories operation.

text.p: Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd said on Wednesday its BHP Steel unit planned to sell the refractory product manufacturing group following a review of operations.
BHP Refractories Pty Ltd general manager Trevor Pennifold told Reuters that the group had annual sales of A$110 million and a carrying value of about A$70 million.

Pennifold said the operations were located in three sites, one near the Newcastle steelworks north of Sydney and two near the Port Kembla steelworks south of Sydney in the state of New South Wales. A sale could take six to nine months, he said, with BHP planning to approach a select number of refractory firms.
"We will be going to a number of refractory companies who we believe might be interested in our business," he said.
BHP Refractories told unions and employees about its sales plans at meetings on Tuesday.
Pennifold said BHP had decided that the refractory product manufacturing group would have a better long term outlook if it was owned by a refractory company rather than a steel company.
